+# Maser design documentation
+
+This folder is Maser's design history: what the product must do, what could go wrong, and how each part is verified.
+It is modeled on the documents a regulated medical device software project keeps, as practice:
+
+- **Software lifecycle:** IEC 62304, including software safety classification and SOUP.
+- **Risk management:** ISO 14971.
+- **Usability engineering:** IEC 62366-1.
+
+Maser isn't a medical device, and nothing here claims compliance with these standards. They are followed for their
+structure and discipline.
+
+**Status: draft 1 (2026-11-03).** This draft covers the features in `main` as of PR #16. It was written after the
+features were built, so it describes the current design rather than having driven it. From here on, a change updates
+these documents in the same PR.
+
+## Documents
+
+| Document | Model | Contents |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| [software-development-plan.md](software-development-plan.md) | IEC 62304 §5.1 | Scope, safety class, lifecycle, SOUP, configuration and problem management, verification strategy |
+| [user-needs.md](user-needs.md) | Design inputs (user needs) | What the user needs Maser to do; validation is against these |
+| [requirements.md](requirements.md) | IEC 62304 §5.2 | Software requirements, each traced to a need and a verification |
+| [risk-management.md](risk-management.md) | ISO 14971 | Harms, hazards, risk estimates, controls and residual risk |
+| [usability.md](usability.md) | IEC 62366-1 | Use specification, user interface characteristics tied to safety, hazard-related use scenarios, evaluations |
+| [traceability.md](traceability.md) | Traceability | Needs → requirements → verification, hazards → controls, and the gaps |
+| [../verification/](../verification/) | Verification records | Dated records of verification runs |
+
+## Identifiers
+
+IDs are permanent. When an item is withdrawn, it is marked `Withdrawn` rather than deleted or renumbered, so links
+from tests, commits and records stay valid.
+
+| Prefix | Item | Example |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `UN-n` | User need | `UN-4` |
+| `REQ-AREA-nnn` | Software requirement | `REQ-CMT-001` |
+| `H-n` | Harm | `H2` |
+| `HAZ-nn` | Hazard (with its sequence of events) | `HAZ-02` |
+| `RC-nn` | Risk control measure | `RC-04` |
+| `HRUS-n` | Hazard-related use scenario | `HRUS-1` |
+| `V-YYYY-MM-DD/Vn` | One check in a verification record | `V-2026-11-03/V10` |
+
+The requirement areas are:
+
+| Area | Covers |
+| --- | --- |
+| `GH` | GitHub access |
+| `QUE` | Queue |
+| `WIN` | Main window |
+| `OVR` | Overview tab |
+| `DIF` | Diff and Files tab |
+| `CMT` | Commenting and reviewing |
+| `KEY` | Keyboard |
+| `CFG` | Configuration |
+| `PLT` | Platform and packaging |
+
+Verification references use these forms:
+
+| Reference | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `T:Suite.test` | Unit test in `MaserCoreTests` |
+| `L:Suite.test` | Live test against GitHub (`MASER_LIVE_TESTS` or `MASER_LIVE_WRITE_TESTS`) |
+| `UI:scenario` | Scripted UI scenario. The harness doesn't exist yet, so these are planned. |
+| `V-…/Vn` | A check in a verification record |
+| `I:` | Inspection of the code or the product |
+| `U:` | Use by the user, recorded in a verification record or a PR |
+
+## Changing these documents
+
+- A PR that changes behavior updates the affected requirements, the risk file if a hazard or control changes, and the
+  traceability, in the same PR. Its description says which IDs it touches.
+- A new requirement says how it will be verified before it is built.
+- A risk control that isn't built yet is a requirement with status `Proposed` and a GitHub issue.
+- The traceability matrix is maintained by hand for now. The plan is a checker in `scripts/check` that builds it from
+  these documents and the tests, and fails on broken or missing links.

+Modeled on IEC 62304 §5.2. Draft 1, 2026-11-03, covering `main` as of PR #16.
+
+Each requirement lists:
+
+- **Need:** the user need it serves.
+- **Control:** the risk control it implements, if any.
+- **Verified by:** how it's verified. **Gap** means it has no repeatable verification yet; most gaps are planned UI
+  scenarios.
+- **Status:**
+  - `Implemented`: built and in `main`.
+  - `Proposed`: a risk control not built yet. It has an issue, and its hazard's residual risk depends on it.
+
+Reference forms are explained in [README.md](README.md#identifiers).

+# Risk management file
+
+Modeled on ISO 14971. Draft 1, 2026-11-03, covering `main` as of PR #16.
+
+## Scope
+
+This file covers Maser as described in the [software development plan](software-development-plan.md): reviewing
+GitHub pull requests on macOS through `gh`. The risks are those of the review tool itself, not of the software being
+reviewed. That software's own risks are managed by the projects that own it. Maser's part is whether it presents the
+change faithfully and acts only as the user intends.
+
+## Harms
+
+| ID | Harm | Severity |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| H1 | A defect in reviewed software goes unnoticed and ships, because the review rested on wrong or incomplete information, or approved code the reviewer never saw. | S4 Critical |
+| H2 | An action the user didn't intend appears under their name, such as an approval, a "Request changes" or a comment, and misleads colleagues or becomes part of a record. | S3 Serious |
+| H3 | Review work the user wrote is lost and has to be redone, or is skipped. | S2 Minor |
+| H4 | The user's GitHub credentials, or their account, are compromised. | S4 Critical |
+| H5 | Time is lost to a hang, crash or confusing behavior, with no lasting effect. | S1 Negligible |
+| H6 | Feedback goes to the wrong place (a different line, file or PR), or never arrives, and the author acts on it wrongly or never sees it. | S3 Serious |
+
+## Risk estimation
+
+**Severity:**
+
+| Level | Name | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| S1 | Negligible | Inconvenience |
+| S2 | Minor | Work redone |
+| S3 | Serious | A wrong or misleading action in a shared record, which others may act on |
+| S4 | Critical | A defect ships, or the account is compromised |
+
+**Probability of the harm**, per use of the feature over the tool's life:
+
+| Level | Name | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| P1 | Improbable | Not expected to happen |
+| P2 | Remote | Could happen, but not expected |
+| P3 | Occasional | Expected to happen now and then |
+| P4 | Probable | Expected often |
+| P5 | Frequent | Routine |
+
+Software failures can't be given meaningful numeric probabilities, as IEC 62304 notes. These estimates are
+qualitative. They are based on how often the hazardous situation arises and how likely it is to lead to the harm.
+Where a failure has actually been seen, such as a crash or a focus bug during the 2026-11-03 sessions, the estimate is
+at least P3 before controls.
+
+**Acceptability.** Each cell is the risk level for a severity and probability:
+
+|  | S1 | S2 | S3 | S4 |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| **P5** | Medium | High | High | High |
+| **P4** | Low | Medium | High | High |
+| **P3** | Low | Medium | Medium | High |
+| **P2** | Low | Low | Medium | Medium |
+| **P1** | Low | Low | Low | Medium |
+
+The levels mean:
+
+- **Low:** acceptable.
+- **Medium:** acceptable only once reduced as far as practicable, with the reason recorded.
+- **High:** not acceptable. The feature needs further controls before it can be relied on.
+
+## Hazard analysis
+
+Each row lists:
+
+- the hazard and the sequence of events that leads to harm;
+- the risk before controls (initial) and after them (residual);
+- the controls, which are detailed in the next section.
+
+| ID | Hazard and sequence of events | Harm | Initial | Controls | Residual |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| HAZ-01 | The diff Maser shows doesn't match the PR: a parse error, a truncated list, a mangled path, or a full-file merge that doesn't fit. The user approves code they didn't actually see. | H1 | S4 P3 **High** | RC-01, RC-02, RC-03 | S4 P1 Medium |
+| HAZ-02 | The PR's head moves (a new push) after Maser loaded the diff. A line comment posted with old line numbers lands on a different line of the new head, or an approval covers commits the user never saw. Maser neither pins the commit nor warns. | H1, H6 | S4 P3 **High** | RC-04 (*proposed*), RC-17 (partial) | **S4 P3 High: open** |
+| HAZ-03 | The user comments on a line that's only shown in the full-file view. GitHub silently creates nothing, and the user believes they raised the issue. | H6 | S3 P4 **High** | RC-05 | S3 P1 Low |
+| HAZ-04 | A key acts somewhere the user didn't expect. For example, `S`, `c` or Return acts on the open PR while the user is looking at a different, highlighted PR in the queue, or on the wrong pane. Several focus bugs of this kind were found on 2026-11-03 (V8–V10). | H2, H6 | S3 P4 **High** | RC-06, RC-12 (*proposed*) | S3 P2 Medium |
+| HAZ-05 | The wrong verdict is submitted, such as Approve instead of Comment, or on the wrong PR. | H2, H1 | S4 P2 Medium | RC-07, RC-12 (*proposed*) | S4 P1 Medium |

+
+## Risk controls
+
+The verification for each control is the verification of its requirements, in [requirements.md](requirements.md).
+
+| ID | Control | Type | Requirements | Status |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| RC-01 | The diff parser is verified against the diff shapes GitHub produces: renames, binary files, the no-newline marker, quoted paths. | Inherent safety by design | REQ-DIF-001 | Implemented |
+| RC-02 | Every paged list is fetched in full, and truncation is detected rather than shown as complete. | Inherent safety by design | REQ-GH-003, REQ-OVR-001 | Implemented |
+| RC-03 | A full file is merged only if its contents match the diff; otherwise Maser shows an error. | Protective measure | REQ-DIF-002 | Implemented |
+| RC-04 | Comments and reviews are pinned to the head commit the user saw, with a warning and a reload when the head has moved. | Protective measure | REQ-CMT-007 | **Proposed** |
+| RC-05 | Expanded lines can't take comments, and say why. A comment GitHub doesn't create is shown as an error. | Protective measure | REQ-DIF-003, REQ-CMT-005 | Implemented |
+| RC-06 | Key ownership is explicit. The window tracks whether the queue or the review has the keys, the open PR is marked, vim keys pause while typing, and `/` acts only in the queue. | Protective measure | REQ-WIN-002, REQ-WIN-003, REQ-KEY-002, REQ-KEY-003 | Implemented |
+| RC-07 | The verdict starts at Comment every time and must be chosen explicitly. Submitting takes a button or ⌘↩ in the sheet. | Protective measure | REQ-CMT-003 | Implemented |
+| RC-08 | Discarding a review asks for confirmation, naming the number of drafts it deletes. | Protective measure | REQ-CMT-004 | Implemented |
+| RC-09 | The UI avoids the layouts that loop AppKit's constraint updates (nested split views, an inspector beside the file tree), and a stress scenario checks for it. | Inherent safety by design | REQ-WIN-007 | Implemented; scenario planned |
+| RC-10 | Unsent text is saved locally as it's typed, and restored. | Protective measure | REQ-CMT-008 | **Proposed** |
+| RC-11 | GitHub access only through `gh`. Maser never handles the token. | Inherent safety by design | REQ-GH-001 | Implemented |
+| RC-12 | The PR and the account are named wherever Maser posts. | Information for safety | REQ-CMT-009 | **Proposed** |
+| RC-13 | `gh` is found by a fixed, documented search order, or by an explicit configured path. | Protective measure | REQ-GH-002 | Implemented |
+| RC-14 | Defensive decoding; failures become messages, per section in the queue. | Protective measure | REQ-GH-004, REQ-QUE-004 | Implemented |
+| RC-15 | Subprocesses never block the UI. | Protective measure | REQ-GH-005 | Implemented (only the login-shell lookup has a timeout) |
+| RC-16 | Rendered PR content runs no JavaScript, and links open in the default browser. | Inherent safety by design | REQ-OVR-002 | Implemented |
+| RC-17 | Data freshness: relative times are refreshed, a PR reloads on return when over 60 s old, and there's a manual refresh (`r`). | Protective measure | REQ-OVR-003, REQ-WIN-001 | Implemented |
+| RC-18 | Config problems are reported in a banner and skipped, never silently applied. Shadowed bindings are reported. | Information for safety | REQ-CFG-002 | Implemented |
+| RC-19 | Live write tests are hard-coded to bmannakee/maser#1, which `AGENTS.md` requires. | Process control | — (I: `LiveReviewWriteTests`) | Implemented |
+| RC-20 | Comment targets are computed from the parsed line numbers on each side, and clipped to one hunk. | Inherent safety by design | REQ-CMT-001 | Implemented |
+
+## Residual risk
+
+The residual risks that are Medium are acceptable only with a reason, recorded here:
+
+- **HAZ-01, HAZ-05, HAZ-08, HAZ-09, HAZ-13:** these are Medium because the harm is Critical, even at Improbable.
+  Further reduction would mean independent verification of the diff against the GitHub web view, or of `gh` itself,
+  which isn't practicable for a client of `gh`. GitHub's own branch protection and other reviewers remain controls on
+  H1.
+- **HAZ-04:** Medium until RC-12 names the PR when posting. The key-routing controls (RC-06) are verified only by one
+  scripted run so far, so the UI harness should make that run repeatable.
+- **HAZ-11:** Medium. A "loaded at" indicator on the Overview would reduce it further. It's recorded as a candidate
+  control, not yet a requirement.
+
+The open risks need further controls before Maser is relied on for review at work:
+
+| Hazard | Residual | Needs | Issue |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| HAZ-02 | High | RC-04: pin comments and reviews to the commit seen, and warn when the head has moved | #18 |
+| HAZ-07 | Medium | RC-10: keep unsent text across crashes and quits | #19 |
+| HAZ-10 (and HAZ-04, HAZ-05) | Medium | RC-12: name the PR and account when posting | #20 |
+| HAZ-12 | Low (observation) | Timeouts on `gh` calls, which have none today, so a hung `gh` loads forever | #21 |
+
+**Overall residual risk:** not yet acceptable for use at work, because HAZ-02 is High. It is acceptable for personal
+use, where reviews carry less weight, provided the user reloads before submitting.
+
+## Production and post-production
+
+Any problem found in use is a GitHub issue. If it reveals a new hazard, or a control that doesn't work, this file is
+updated in the PR that fixes it. The 2026-11-03 crashes and focus bugs are recorded this way: as evidence for HAZ-04
+and HAZ-07, and through RC-06 and RC-09.

+# Software development plan
+
+Modeled on IEC 62304 §5.1. Draft 1, 2026-11-03.
+
+## Scope and intended use
+
+**Maser is a native macOS app for reviewing GitHub pull requests.** It lists the PRs needing the user's attention,
+shows a PR's conversation, status and changes, and lets the user comment on lines, reply to threads, and submit a
+review with a verdict. It does everything through the user's own `gh` command-line client.
+
+**Intended user:** one experienced software engineer, the author, who works mostly from the keyboard with vim-style
+keys. See [usability.md](usability.md) for the full use specification.
+
+**Intended use environment:**
+
+- The user's personal Mac: macOS 27.
+- An enterprise-managed work Mac: macOS 26, with only the Xcode command-line tools, and no unsigned or quarantined
+  apps.
+- github.com, and potentially GitHub Enterprise hosts.
+
+**Why it matters:** at work, Maser will be used to review software that may itself be regulated. A review decision
+made on wrong or incomplete information can let a defect through. Code review isn't the only control on that software,
+but Maser should not weaken it. This is the main source of harm in the [risk file](risk-management.md).
+
+## Software safety classification
+
+**Class B, for practice.**
+
+IEC 62304 classifies by the worst harm that a failure of the software could contribute to, after external risk
+controls. Maser can't injure anyone directly. A failure could, however, contribute to a defect in reviewed software
+going unnoticed, as described in `H1` in the risk file. Other controls on that software lie outside Maser: other
+reviewers, testing, and the work organization's own quality system.
+
+On a strict reading that makes Maser Class A. It is treated as **Class B** to practice the extra activities Class B
+requires:
+
+- architectural design documentation;
+- documented software units with verification;
+- integration testing;
+- regression testing.
+
+## Lifecycle
+
+| Activity | How it's done |
+| --- | --- |
+| Planning | This plan; GitHub issues for planned work |
+| Requirements | [requirements.md](requirements.md), updated in the PR that changes behavior |
+| Architecture | `AGENTS.md` ("Architecture"): `MaserCore` (testable logic, GitHub access) and `Maser` (views, view models) |
+| Detailed design | Doc comments on every type and function, as `AGENTS.md` requires; file header comments |
+| Implementation | Swift 6, strict concurrency; conventions in `AGENTS.md`; formatting enforced by `swift format` |
+| Unit verification | Swift Testing in `MaserCoreTests`; `scripts/check` runs them on every commit |
+| Integration verification | Live tests against GitHub (`MASER_LIVE_TESTS=1`; `MASER_LIVE_WRITE_TESTS=1`, limited to bmannakee/maser#1). The scripted UI harness is planned. |
+| System verification | Scripted UI scenarios (planned); verification records in `docs/verification/` |
+| Validation | Use by the intended user against [user-needs.md](user-needs.md), recorded per release |
+| Release | `scripts/bundle` builds `Maser.app`. Planned: a tagged release and a release record listing what was verified, with known anomalies. |
+
+Every change goes through a branch and a PR. Nothing is committed to `main` directly. Review usually happens in Maser
+itself. PR descriptions follow `AGENTS.md`:
+
+- **Summary**
+- **Implementation notes**
+- **Testing**, including what wasn't checked by hand
+
+## SOUP (software of unknown provenance)
+
+| Item | Version | Use | Known risks and how they're handled |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| GitHub CLI (`gh`) | 2.102.1 at home; work version unknown | All GitHub access, authentication and the token | Output format changes break decoding. Handled by decoding defensively (`REQ-GH-004`), live tests, and showing failures as messages. |
+| GitHub GraphQL and REST APIs | — | Data and mutations | Quiet failures. A comment on a line outside the diff returns a null thread (`HAZ-03`). Lists are capped (`HAZ-14`). |
+| TOMLDecoder | 0.4.5 (`Package.resolved`) | Parsing `config.toml` | Decode errors surface as `TOMLError`; the config banner reports them (`REQ-CFG-002`). |
+| SwiftUI and AppKit | macOS 26 / 27 SDKs | UI | Layout loops crashed the app when split views were nested, or with an inspector beside the file tree (`HAZ-07`, V5–V7). Focus doesn't always move when asked (V9). |
+| WebKit | macOS SDK | Rendering the conversation HTML | Untrusted content. Page JavaScript is disabled (`REQ-OVR-002`). |
+| Swift toolchain | 6.2 minimum; 6.4 at home | Build | The work Mac's version is unknown, so the minimum is checked by building against `swift-tools-version: 6.2`. |
+
+## Configuration management
+
+- **Source:** git, at `github.com/bmannakee/maser`.
+- **Dependencies:** pinned by `Package.resolved`.
+- **Build identity:** the bundle's version is `git describe --tags --always` at build time. A build from uncommitted
+  changes reports the last commit. That happened during verification on 2026-11-03, so releases must be built from a
+  clean tree.
+
+## Problem resolution
+
+Problems are GitHub issues. An issue that turns out to be a risk, such as a crash or a wrong action, is linked to its
+hazard in the risk file, and the PR that fixes it updates the risk file.
+
+## Verification strategy
+
+| Level | What | When |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Unit | `MaserCoreTests` | Every commit (`scripts/check`) |
+| Integration, read | Live read tests | Before merging changes to GitHub access |
+| Integration, write | Live write tests on PR #1 only | Before merging changes to write paths |
+| System (UI) | Scripted scenarios with a fake `gh` (planned) | Every commit, once built |
+| Validation | Use by the intended user | Before each release |
+
+A requirement that can't be tested automatically says so and names its inspection or manual check.

+# Usability engineering file
+
+Modeled on IEC 62366-1. Draft 1, 2026-11-03.
+
+## Use specification
+
+- **Intended use:** reviewing GitHub pull requests: reading the change and its context, commenting, and submitting a
+  verdict. The full statement is in the [software development plan](software-development-plan.md#scope-and-intended-use).
+- **User profile:**
+  - One user: an experienced software engineer, and the author of Maser.
+  - Expert with git, GitHub and the terminal.
+  - Prefers the keyboard, with vim-style keys and multi-key sequences.
+  - Reviews many PRs, often several in one sitting, at home and at work.
+  - At work, the reviewed software may be regulated.
+- **Use environment:**
+  - macOS desktop, often with several windows and apps open.
+  - Long sessions.
+  - Interruptions: a review may be left half-written and resumed later.
+  - The work Mac is managed, and the user can't change system settings such as the key-repeat rate.
+- **Operating principle:**
+  - The queue in a sidebar, with the open PR's review beside it.
+  - Each review has an Overview tab (conversation and status) and a Files tab (file tree, diff with a line cursor, and
+    comments).
+  - Every action is a command, available as a menu shortcut, vim-style keys, or both.
+
+## User interface characteristics related to safety
+
+These are the parts of the interface where a use error could lead to a hazard in the [risk file](risk-management.md).
+
+| ID | Characteristic | Related hazards |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| UIC-1 | **Two places can have the keys,** the queue or the review, and the same key (`j`, `k`, `]`, `[`, `o`, `r`, Return) does different things in each. The queue's selection and the open PR can differ. | HAZ-04, HAZ-05 |
+| UIC-2 | **Single-key commands with effects:** `c` (comment), `R` (reply), `S` (Finish Review). A stray key can start an action. | HAZ-04 |
+| UIC-3 | **Multi-key sequences** (`g g`, `z a`, `g p`). A half-typed sequence waits up to 1.5 s for the next key. | HAZ-04 |
+| UIC-4 | **Two views of a file,** hunks and full. In the full view, some lines can't take comments. | HAZ-03 |
+| UIC-5 | **Pending versus posted.** Line comments are private drafts until the review is submitted, but replies post at once when there's no pending review. | HAZ-04, HAZ-07 |
+| UIC-6 | **The verdict choice** in Finish Review: Comment, Approve or Request changes. | HAZ-05 |
+| UIC-7 | **Configurable keys.** The user's bindings can differ from the defaults and from the docs. | HAZ-16 |
+
+## Hazard-related use scenarios
+
+| ID | Scenario | Hazard | Controls | Evaluation |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| HRUS-1 | The user moves through the queue with `j`/`k`, sees a PR highlighted, then presses `S` or `c` believing it acts on the highlighted PR. It acts on the open PR, which is the same one only if the selection has settled. | HAZ-04 | RC-06; RC-12 (proposed) | V-2026-11-03/V10 (routing). Not yet evaluated with the user. |
+| HRUS-2 | After clicking in the sidebar, the user presses `c` to comment. Before 2026-11-03 the queue swallowed it with a beep; afterwards, focus jumped back to the queue mid-comment. | HAZ-04 | RC-06 | FE-2, FE-3. Fixed and re-checked (V8). |
+| HRUS-3 | The user reaches for `[` `]` `{` `}` and presses `/` by mistake, moving focus to the queue's filter. | HAZ-04 | RC-06 (`/` only in the queue) | FE-4. Fixed and re-checked (V10). |
+| HRUS-4 | In the full-file view, the user comments on a line outside the diff. | HAZ-03 | RC-05 | L:LiveReviewWriteTests (error). The notice wording hasn't been evaluated with the user. |
+| HRUS-5 | In Finish Review, the user means to Comment, but the radio group is left on Approve or set there by a stray key, and they press ⌘↩. | HAZ-05 | RC-07; RC-12 (proposed) | Not yet evaluated. |
+| HRUS-6 | The user writes a long reply, switches to another PR or app, then quits or Maser crashes. | HAZ-07 | RC-09; RC-10 (proposed) | FE-1 (crashes observed). |
+| HRUS-7 | The user reviews at work while `gh` is signed in to their personal account. | HAZ-10 | RC-12 (proposed) | Not yet evaluated. |
+| HRUS-8 | The user reviews a PR, a colleague pushes, and the user submits an approval without reloading. | HAZ-02 | RC-04 (proposed) | Not yet evaluated. |
+
+## Formative evaluations
+
+These were informal: the intended user, using a build on the home Mac.
+
+| ID | Date | Build / PR | What the user did | Finding | Outcome |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| FE-1 | 2026-11-03 | #16 (f3d28d3) | Switched to Files with `g f` in the new main window | Crash, twice (V5) | Fixed in #16 (V6, V7) |
+| FE-2 | 2026-11-03 | #16 | Clicked a PR, then pressed `c` and `g f` | The keys beeped; the queue swallowed them | Unused keys now go on to the review (#16) |
+| FE-3 | 2026-11-03 | #16 | Pressed `c` on Overview, and `j` then `c` on Files | Overview: nothing. Files: focus jumped back to the queue | `defaultFocus` removed (V8) |
+| FE-4 | 2026-11-03 | #16 | Pressed `/` by accident, and ⌘0 | `/` moved focus to the filter; ⌘0 didn't give the queue the keys | Explicit key ownership, and `/` only in the queue (V9, V10) |
+| FE-5 | 2026-11-03 | #16 | Opened the Files tab | Side panes much too wide; the diff squeezed | Fixed widths (#16) |
+| FE-6 | 2026-11-03 | #13 | Held `j`/`k` | Slow and jittery | Fixed in #13 (V2). The remaining limit is the key-repeat rate. |
+
+## Summative evaluation (planned)
+
+Before relying on Maser for review at work, run each HRUS above with the user on a release build, against a test PR.
+For each one, record whether the use error happened, and whether the user noticed it before harm. The prerequisites
+are:
+
+- the open risks in the risk file are controlled, especially RC-04 and RC-12;

+# User needs
+
+What the user needs from Maser, in their terms. Requirements trace back to these, and validation shows they're met.
+Draft 1, 2026-11-03.
+
+| ID | Need | Why |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| UN-1 | I can see the pull requests that need my attention as soon as I open the app: ones where my review is requested, ones I wrote, and ones I'm involved in. | Without them the app opens on nothing; finding PRs in a browser is what Maser replaces. |
+| UN-2 | I can read a PR's description, conversation, reviews, checks, labels and merge status, as GitHub shows them. | A review decision needs the whole context, not only the code. |
+| UN-3 | I can read exactly what a PR changes, either as hunks or as the whole file with the changes in place, and trust that it matches GitHub. | Approving code I didn't actually see, or saw wrongly, defeats the review. |
+| UN-4 | I can comment on a line or a range, reply to threads, and submit a review as Comment, Approve or Request changes. My line comments stay private until I submit. | This is the core of reviewing. |
+| UN-5 | I can do all of it from the keyboard with vim-style keys. Keys always act where I expect, with no surprises. | That's how I work fastest. A key acting on the wrong PR or pane is worse than no key. |
+| UN-6 | I can configure keys and behavior in a plain-text file in my dotfiles, and mistakes in it are reported, not silently applied. | I keep my setup in dotfiles across machines. |
+| UN-7 | I can use Maser on my managed work Mac, with macOS 26, no admin rights and no unsigned apps, using the `gh` I already have. | I need it most at work. |
+| UN-8 | Maser never exposes my GitHub credentials, and acts only as me, only on the PR and line I intend. | Actions under my name are visible to my colleagues, and at work they may be part of a regulated record. |
+| UN-9 | I don't lose review work I've written, whether to a crash, a quit or a slip of the keyboard. | Rewriting a careful review is costly, and it gets skipped. |
+| UN-10 | Maser is quick: it opens fast, moves between PRs instantly, and scrolls smoothly. | Slowness pushes me back to the browser. |
